headline: Remulla Estimates First-Year Public School Security Upgrades at ₱5 Billion
seoTitle: Remulla Estimates School Security Upgrades at ₱5 Billion | FMB News
seoDescription: DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla estimated that stronger security systems for public schools could cost about ₱5 billion in the first year.
keywords: public school CCTV metal detectors Philippines
deck: The DILG chief gave the first-year estimate as education and interior officials pursued tighter access controls, surveillance and local security coordination for schools.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla estimated that improving security systems across public schools could cost about ₱5 billion in the first year.

The estimate comes as the Department of Education prepares to provide schools with metal detectors and closed-circuit television systems, tighten security protocols and strengthen coordination with barangay tanods and other local safety personnel.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: DILG and DepEd have been preparing an inter-agency agreement to strengthen security inside and around school premises following recent campus violence. Current government reporting supports the policy direction toward closer local coordination, stronger surveillance and controlled access.

The delivery envelope also described panic alarms, a separate ₱1.2-billion mental-health allocation, a 2027 congressional submission and a fourth-quarter pilot. Those details were not independently established by the accessible cited material and are not presented here as facts.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The estimate signals the potential scale of a nationwide school-security program, but its final cost and scope will depend on formal agency plans and budget approval. Physical safeguards also need trained personnel, clear reporting procedures and student-support measures to avoid creating a climate of fear.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DILG, DepEd and budget authorities for the signed inter-agency agreement, an itemized funding proposal, procurement standards and implementation rules for cameras, metal detectors and local security coordination.
